title: Entanglement Wedge Reconstruction Beyond the Large N Limit via the Twirled Petz Map
authors: Arash Alipour Shahmiri, Maryam Sharifian, Niloofar Vardian
abstract: Entanglement wedge reconstruction provides the sharpest formulation of bulk locality in AdS/CFT, identifying the entanglement wedge as the largest bulk region reconstructible from a boundary subregion. While this statement is well understood at leading order in the large N expansion through both modular flow and Petz map reconstruction, its extension beyond the semiclassical regime has remained unclear. In this work, we show that quantum error correction provides the natural framework for addressing this problem. At leading order, we reproduce the known leading-order reconstruction formulas, and by employing the twirled Petz map, we obtain a systematic and explicit method for incorporating subleading 1/N corrections. Beyond the leading approximation, we have obtained an explicit bi-local correction controlled by a subleading Petz kernel. Our results establish a controlled approach to bulk reconstruction beyond large N and sharpening the role of quantum error correction in holography. This framework provides a controlled path toward understanding bulk reconstruction in fully quantum gravitational settings.
summary: This work extends the concept of Entanglement Wedge Reconstruction in AdS/CFT by employing the framework of Quantum Error Correction. By introducing the 'twirled Petz map,' the authors derive a systematic method to calculate subleading 1/N corrections, thereby providing a controlled theoretical path to understanding bulk physics in fully quantum gravitational regimes.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of extending the Entanglement Wedge Reconstruction (EWR) principle beyond the semiclassical, large N limit in AdS/CFT correspondence.
main_result: The authors provide a systematic and explicit method using the twirled Petz map to incorporate subleading 1/N corrections into bulk reconstruction formulas.
method: The approach utilizes Quantum Error Correction (QEC) theory, specifically generalizing the Petz map to the 'twirled Petz map' to systematically calculate higher-order corrections in the 1/N expansion.
model_or_system: The physical system is the AdS/CFT correspondence, focusing on reconstructing bulk local observables (the entanglement wedge) from boundary quantum field theory data.
key_observables: The explicit bi-local correction controlled by a subleading Petz kernel, and the reconstruction of bulk fields in terms of boundary modular operators.
important_parameters: The large N expansion parameter (1/N), and the subleading quantum gravitational corrections.
main_assumptions: The initial analysis is restricted to semiclassical AdS geometries without horizons, though the framework aims to provide a controlled path toward fully quantum gravitational settings.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of EWR beyond leading order, then grounds the solution in the formalism of Quantum Error Correction (QEC) using the Petz map, and finally applies this generalized map to derive explicit, controlled corrections to the holographic reconstruction formulas.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between QEC theory (a tool from quantum information) and the fundamental structure of spacetime locality (holography) provides a powerful, mathematically controlled framework for understanding quantum gravity effects.
